messages.author: 428d1e2fc2be88d9
messages.subject: Plotting of two block PLS (two.b.pls())
parts:
Dear geomorph R group, 

I am quantifying the evolutionary shape changes of the skull and vertebral column of the salamandrid genus Lissotriton. I assessed the covariation between the skull shape and the first trunk vertebrae by a two block partial least squares analysis. I want to create a ggplot2-plot from the elements produced by the two.b.pls function, as i managed to do so for PCA, PTA and phylomorphospace plots. However I have a hard time figuring out which elements from the two.b.pls output are accessible for ggplot2. Could anyone tell me which elements should be used by ggplot2 and how they have to be constructed in order to produce a plot? 

Thanks in advance and best regards, 

Stefan

messages.author: a5e534225b982050
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] Plotting of two block PLS (two.b.pls())
parts:
Hi Stefan,
If I remember correctly, in the pls object you have $XScores and $YScores that can be used to reproduce the plot. They are matrices and correspond to the scores of X and Y blocs on the different PLS axes, if you want to plot the first PLS axis, you should select the first column of each.
Cheers,
Adrien

messages.author: a5e534225b982050
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] Plotting of two block PLS (two.b.pls())
parts:
Hi Stefan,
Maybe because $XScores and $YScores are already matrices, and ggplot may require two vectors. You could create a dataframe (let's say 'PLS1') with vectors 'PLSobj$XScores[,1]' and 'PLSobj$YScores[,1]', to use in the ggplot function.
PLS1=data.frame(X=PLSobj$XScores[,1],Y=PLSobj$YScores[,1])
then ggplot(PLS1, aes(x=X,y=Y))
Best
A

Adrien is correct. The matrices $Xscores and $Yscores contain the desired components of the the PLS.  The plot produced in geomorph uses the first column of each, as these represent the scores on the first PLS axes.

 

Dean
